pr_comments:
ping @pranavkm and @GrabYourPitchforks before I go much farther for a direction check.  Naming is clearly tbd, but basically I tried adding a new top level interface that extends the existing DataProtection abstractions and adds the Span overloads of Protect/Unprotect, the placeholder name is `ISpanDataProtector` :shrug:

Then I just went and implemented span only APIs where I could, mostly replacing ArraySegement/byte[] apis with span versions.  It looks like for the new Gcm API we just added since its netcore only, we can just stop using the other internal IOptiomizedEncryptor and switch to using spans directly (i think).

Mostly just wanted to get a sense that this looks reasonable before fleshing out all the details.

Updated using default interface methods to avoid any breaks, I did have to add a clunky IsSpanEnabled on the IAuthenticatedEncryptor which is the replacement for checking for a specific interface to tell whether we can use the Span methods in the Protector classes.  

@davidfowl do you want to take a look and review the new Span enabled dataprotection apis?  @pranavkm recommended we engage you early

Note: the public API analyzers were pretty unhappy with these (not sure if its because the APIs only exist in net60 and not netstandard?  @dougbu do you have any ideas if what i'm tyring to do breaks the analyzers?  I just suppressed them for now since I couldn't get the baselines to accept the new apis
Closing after reviewing with David and Levi, will open a new PR

issue_context.title: Spanify DataProtection code
comments: Also address follow up to https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/29814#discussion_r581658453 as part of this issue, and the reg ex issue linked
Will handle any remaning minor span cleanup as part of the PR switching to framework version of PDKDF in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/30941 closing as dupe

review_comments: The existing pattern was to have an internal derived interface IOptimizedAuthenticatedEncryptor, which was the previous iterations equivalent of an internal ISpanAuthenticatedEncryptor.  Then KeyRingDataProtector would try casting as opposed to calling IsSpanEnabled.  I'm sorta ambivalent between the two do you have a strong preference?  The downside of the internal interface is there's no way for anyone else to implement Span enabled encryptors which seems pretty bad which is why I switched this to the default interface method style from IDataProtector, but we need the IsSpanEnabled unless we want to try/catch NotImplementedException or something super gross

Nit: Might want to reverse the order of inputs and outputs:

```suggestion
        bool TryProtect(ReadOnlySpan<byte> plaintext, Span<byte> output, out int bytesWritten)
```
To start I just forked the existing Protect code to call into the Span version of code when available, didn't look to reuse any code between codepaths for now.
This change is from https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/30013 which is unrelated, but we are rolling into this PR
